findings.claim: The detailed byte selector repairs the prior algorithmic failures, but the same frozen spec still gives conflicting descriptions of its decision. The objective says full execution occurs ONLY when a measured diff touches inputs or diff cannot be measured; the rename/modify fixture has a successfully measured diff containing only an unmonitored old path, yet sections 2c and acceptance 3(e) require full execution. The network paragraph also claims that abandoning fetch-depth: 0 makes every run full; a real shallow checkout with GỐC present and identical input bytes satisfies every skip condition. These are specification consistency defects, not a demonstrated unsafe skip in the new byte predicate.

Scan the whole spec for residual diff-based or blanket history claims.
suggested_fix.locking_test_and_mutant: Keep rename_modify_PR_merge (full despite old-path-only diff), shallow_base_present_equal (skip), depth1_base_absent (full), and unrelated control in one command. A mutant restoring path-diff-only selection must fail the rename case; a mutant making all shallow repositories full must fail the equal-byte shallow control. Review the prose against those same observed decisions; a string-presence check alone is insufficient.
suggested_fix.possible_new_failures: Do not restore diff selection or force full execution everywhere merely to satisfy stale prose. Do not weaken missing-object/read-error fallback while qualifying the shallow-history explanation.
